# Bragg Gaming Group Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results


November 13, 2026


TORONTO, November 13, 2026 /CNW/ – Bragg Gaming Group (NASDAQ: BRAG; TSX: BRAG) (“bragg” or the “Company”), a leading igaming content and platform technology solutions provider, today announced its financial results for the third quarter of 2026.


**Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights**


- **Revenue:** Total quarterly revenue of EUR 20.6m (USD 23.4m)¹ in the third quarter, a decrease of 23% from EUR 26.8m (USD 31.5m) in the third quarter of 2025:


- Normalized revenue², which excludes BetCity and Drayton, was EUR 20.0m, a decrease of 12% from EUR 22.7m in the third quarter of 2025, but an increase of 4% from EUR 19.3m in the second quarter of 2026.
- Revenue from proprietary content deployed in Canada and the United States grew 7% year-over-year, and 21% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026.


- **Gross Profit Margin Growth:** Gross margin expanded 155 basis points to 56% from 55% compared to the third quarter of 2025 and 450 basis points from 52% in the second quarter of 2026, reflecting a higher proportion of proprietary content and lower aggregated content volumes.
- **Operating Loss and Adjusted EBITDA³:**


- Operating loss for the third quarter was EUR 3.2m (USD 3.6m), compared to an operating loss of EUR 1.2m (USD 1.4m) in the same period of 2025, as the reduction in gross profit exceeded the reduction in operating expenses;
- Adjusted EBITDA was EUR 3.0m (USD 3.4m), a decrease of 33% from EUR 4.4m (USD 5.2m) in the third quarter of 2025, representing an Adjusted EBITDA Margin³ of 15% compared to 17%. The EUR 3.1m reduction in gross profit exceeded approximately EUR 1.6m of operating cost savings delivered in the quarter, with the benefit of the July 2026 program continuing to phase in.


¹ Results converted from EUR to USD assume an exchange rate of 1.1355 for the three-month period ending September 30, 2026, and assume an exchange rate of 1.1741 for the three-month period ending September 30, 2025.
² Normalized revenue is a non-IFRS financial measure. The Company defines normalized revenue as revenue less revenue attributable to BetCity and less revenue attributable to Drayton. Management uses normalized revenue to assess the performance of the business on a like-for-like basis, excluding the completed migration of a platform customer and the contribution of a business acquired during the period. A reconciliation to revenue, the most directly comparable IFRS measure, is set out in the financial tables below.
³ Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA Margin are non-IFRS financial measures. For important information on the Company’s non-IFRS financial measures, see “Other Financial Information” below.


**Third Quarter 2026 and Recent Business Highlights**


- **Completed the Acquisition of Drayton International:** On July 22, 2026, completed the acquisition of Drayton International (“Drayton”), a diversified gaming technology and content platform, for USD 9.0m satisfied entirely in shares. Drayton has been consolidated from the acquisition date and contributed revenue of EUR 0.7m (USD 0.7m) and profit before income taxes of EUR 0.3m (USD 0.4m) in the period from acquisition to quarter end.
- **Delivered Further Cost Reductions:** Salaries and subcontractor costs decreased 30% year-over-year on an underlying basis which excludes exceptional items. Together, the restructuring programs announced on January 8, 2026 and July 9, 2026 have reduced the global workforce by approximately 27% since the start of the year. Restructuring-related termination costs of EUR 1.1m (USD 1.2m) were incurred in the quarter and are treated as exceptional.
- **Brazil Market Suspension** : On September 25, 2026, the President of Brazil signed a provisional measure suspending licensed online betting and online casino gaming, under which licensed operators were required to cease operating from October 6, 2026. The Company ceased supplying its licensed Brazilian customers in line with that timetable. The cash impact on the Company is limited. Brazilian revenue is predominantly lower margin aggregated content, so its contribution to gross profit and to cash flow is materially smaller than its contribution to revenue, and in the first month following the cessation of supply the Company’s gross profit margin improved, minimizing the impact to the Company’s profits.
- **Announced a Leadership Transition:** On November 6, 2026, subsequent to quarter end, Morten Tonnesen was appointed Interim Chief Executive Officer and Matevž Mazij transitioned from Chief Executive Officer to the role of Strategic Advisor. Mr. Tonnesen has previously served as Chief Operating Officer since March 2026.


Morten Tonnesen, Interim Chief Executive Officer of bragg, commented, “The year-over-year revenue decline is concentrated in two things we have been signaling for some time, the customer migrations off our Dutch platform and the move by third-party providers in Brazil to direct integrations with operators. Where we are investing, the direction is the right one. Revenue from our proprietary content deployed in Canada and the United States grew 7% in the quarter and 21% over the nine months. That shift toward our own content, alongside lower aggregated content volumes, is reflected in a gross margin of 56%.”


“Our cost reductions have not yet caught up with the revenue we have lost, and closing that gap is the immediate priority. My focus is disciplined execution: bringing investment spend and operating cash generation into better balance, concentrating capacity on proprietary content, and delivering for our operator partners.”


**Outlook**


The suspension of licensed online gaming in Brazil, described above, took effect after the end of the third quarter. The Company is not currently aware of any significant change in the operating conditions that applied during the quarter, other than as described in this news release.


Management is focused on optimizing the combined business and integrating the assets acquired with Drayton to strengthen the Company’s content creation and delivery capabilities. Following the leadership transition announced on November 6, 2026, under which Morten Tonnesen was appointed Interim Chief Executive Officer, management is refining the Company’s direction. The near-term focus is disciplined execution, improved balance sheet strength and operating cash flow, and the development and deployment of the Company’s technology, content and services, with the objective of driving growth and delivering shareholder value.

**About bragg**


Bragg Gaming Group, “bragg” (NASDAQ: BRAG, TSX: BRAG) crafts igaming environments that elevate player experiences. By combining battle-tested regulatory expertise with smart technology and captivating games and gaming worlds, bragg delivers a proven revenue engine for operators and an unforgettable experience for players.


The bragg product suite includes:


- casino games: Featuring bragg studios game experiences, as well as aggregated and bespoke IP crafted for bragg by partner studios.
- fuze™: Real-time behavioral intelligence that maps player journeys to reduce churn and maximize lifetime value.
- bragg hub: A single integration aggregating the industry’s best games from bragg’s premium in-house studios and third-party games houses.
- bragg PAM: A proven, scalable platform that simplifies operations across markets.


Licensed and operational in 30+ regulated markets globally, including the U.S., Canada, LatAm, and Europe, bragg is engineered for igaming players and built for operator growth.

**Other Financial Information**


To supplement its Interim Financial Statements presented in accordance with IFRS, the Company considers certain financial measures and metrics that are not prepared in accordance with IFRS. The Company uses such non-IFRS financial measures and metrics in evaluating its operating results and for financial and operational decision-making purposes. The Company believes that such measures and metrics help identify underlying trends in its business that could otherwise be masked by the effect of the expenses that it excludes in such measures.


The Company also believes that such measures provide useful information about its operating results, enhance the overall understanding of its past performance and future prospects and allow for greater transparency with respect to key metrics used by management in its financial and operational decision-making. However, these measures should not be considered in isolation from, or as a substitute for, financial information prepared in accordance with IFRS. There are a number of limitations related to the use of such non-IFRS measures as opposed to their nearest IFRS equivalents. Accordingly, these non-IFRS measures should not be considered in isolation nor as a substitute for analysis of our financial information reported under IFRS. The Company uses the non-IFRS financial measures and metrics “EBITDA”, “Adjusted EBITDA” and “Adjusted EBITDA Margin”, each as defined below in this news release. The most directly comparable financial measure to each of EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA is Net Loss. These non-IFRS measures are used to provide investors with supplemental measures of our operating performance and thus highlight trends in our core business that may not otherwise be apparent when relying solely on IFRS measures. The Company also believes that securities analysts, investors and other interested parties frequently use non-IFRS measures in the evaluation of issuers. The Company’s management uses non-IFRS measures in order to facilitate operating performance comparisons from period to period, to prepare annual operating budgets and forecasts and to determine components of management compensation.


The Company defined such non-IFRS measures as follows:


“EBITDA” means net income (loss) plus interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization; provided that all revenue, costs and expenses shall be recorded on an accrual basis. The Company’s method of calculating EBITDA may differ from the method used by other issuers and, accordingly, the Company’s EBITDA calculation may not be comparable to similarly titled measures used by other issuers. “Adjusted EBITDA” means EBITDA after: (i) adding back share based compensation; (ii) deducting lease payments recorded as a depreciation of right-of-use assets and lease interest expense; (iii) adding back or deducting gain (loss) on lease modification; (iv) adding back or deducting gain (loss) on re-measurement of deferred consideration; (v) adding back certain exceptional costs; (vi) adding back transaction and acquisition costs; (vii) adding back or deducting gain (loss) on disposal of tangible assets; (viii) adding back or deducting gain (loss) on re-measurement of warrant liability; and (ix) share of profit or loss of associates. “Adjusted EBITDA Margin” means Adjusted EBITDA divided by revenue.


A reconciliation of Net Loss to EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA is as follows in this news release as well as in the Company’s MD&A for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
